why: SHARE TEMPLATE. The source machine's allowlist maps real working-session ids to the telemetry files that session's suite runs polluted; those ids point at transcripts nobody else can open, so `session_files` ships empty. The schema is unchanged. Scope is per FILE, not per session: a session that ran a suite also did real work, so a session-wide skip would hide real rows. `literals` are synthetic session_id VALUES a suite writes on purpose (synthtest-transport, selftest, calib, probe) and are skipped in every file. Extend `session_files`, never mutate a .jsonl, when a suite-contaminated (session, file) pair is identified on your own machine. KNOWN LIMIT: a genuine deny by a listed session in a listed file is skipped with the suite rows; the count cannot tell them apart.
